steps.message:
The build succeeds. Here's the patch and reasoning:

## Root cause

In `ManageLocationFragment.goToManageFishingSpot()`:

```java
List<UserDefineObject> allPossibleFishingSpots = mFishingSpots;   // alias, not a copy!
mFishingSpots.addAll(getNewLocation().getFishingSpots());          // mutates the real list
```

`allPossibleFishingSpots` was only supposed to be a convenience list handed to the spot dialog (used to center the map). But it aliased `mFishingSpots`, and the next line appended *the location's spots re-read from the database* into that very same list.

When editing a location, the "new" `Location` is a copy created with `keepId = true`, so `getNewLocation().getFishingSpots()` returns exactly the spots already held in `mFishingSpots` (fresh objects with the *same* IDs). Every time the user tapped a spot, `mFishingSpots` became `[A, A']`.

Then on save of the spot:

```java
for (int i = 0; i < mFishingSpots.size(); i++)
    if (mFishingSpots.get(i).getId().equals(...)) { mFishingSpots.set(i, updated); return true; }
```

only the *first* match was replaced, leaving the stale duplicate `A'` (with the old coordinates) in the list — hence "two of the same spot in the list" and "the coordinates of the existing fishing spot are not updated". The second save appeared correct only because the duplicate rows collapsed on insert.

## Fix

1. Pass a **copy** of the spot list to the dialog and drop the duplicating `addAll` (it was redundant — the DB query returns the spots `mFishingSpots` already holds, and for a brand-new location it returns nothing):

```java
List<UserDefineObject> allPossibleFishingSpots = new ArrayList<UserDefineObject>(mFishingSpots);
fragment.setFishingSpots(allPossibleFishingSpots);
```

2. Clear `mFishingSpotViews` in `updateAllFishingSpots()` after detaching the old views, so the cached view list matches what's actually in the container instead of accumulating stale views on every rebuild.

With this, editing a spot updates the single existing entry in place with the new coordinates, and no phantom duplicate is added.

mFishingSpots.addAll(getNewLocation().getFishingSpots());          // mutates the real list

Then on save of the spot:

```java
for (int i = 0; i < mFishingSpots.size(); i++)
    if (mFishingSpots.get(i).getId().equals(...)) { mFishingSpots.set(i, updated); return true; }
```

only the *first* match was replaced, leaving the stale duplicate `A'` (with the old coordinates) in the list — hence "two of the same spot in the list" and "the coordinates of the existing fishing spot are not updated". The second save appeared correct only because the duplicate rows collapsed on insert.

1. Pass a **copy** of the spot list to the dialog and drop the duplicating `addAll` (it was redundant — the DB query returns the spots `mFishingSpots` already holds, and for a brand-new location it returns nothing):
